<details open>

metal : support BF16/F32 src1 for MUL_MAT and MUL_MAT_ID (#32677)

* llama, metal : support BF16 src1 for MUL_MAT and MUL_MAT_ID

Add GGML_PREC_BF16 handling for src1 on the Metal backend when the tensor
API is available: MUL_MAT with an F32 src0 stages the A tile as bfloat, and
MUL_MAT_ID stages src1 as bfloat instead of F16. The tensor path keeps src1
in F32 when it reads the operand directly.

Add a temporary LLAMA_MOE_AMAX_SKIP env var that disables the graph-level
amax rescaling for the MoE down projection and sets the BF16 src1 hint
instead. Apply the hint inside build_lora_mm_id so it reaches the matmul
before the per-expert scale and LoRA nodes wrap it.

Add MUL_MAT_ID src1 BF16 test cases to test-backend-ops.

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB)

* metal : support BF16 src1 without the tensor API

Allow GGML_PREC_BF16 when the device has bfloat, not only when it has the
Metal4 tensor API.

Add legacy _prec_bf16 kernels for MUL_MAT and MUL_MAT_ID that stage src1 as
bfloat in the threadgroup and run the simdgroup multiply with bfloat A and B.
The F16 MUL_MAT_ID kernel uses half A on the tensor path and bfloat A on the
legacy path.

Cast the quantized dequantize outputs to the destination element type: the
older Metal compiler on M2 rejects implicit float to bfloat.

Tested on M2 Ultra (legacy): MUL_MAT_PREC_SRC1 24/24 and
MUL_MAT_ID_PREC_SRC1_BF16 30/30. Flint Q4_K_M with LLAMA_MOE_AMAX_SKIP=1:
pp512 -2.1%, tg128 +25.5% vs master. On M5 Max: pp512 +2.1%, tg128 +22.2%.

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB)

first: a short plain-language line on what the command does. The tool

ggml-openvino: CI fixes, new model support, fixes and improvements. (#32861)

* ggml-openvino: keep the rope angle in f32 under the f16 inference hint

* ggml-openvino: add a GGML_OP_ARGMAX translator

* ggml-openvino: keep the token dim dynamic for a 2-D activation graph input

* ggml-openvino: tolerate graph inputs and outputs with no backing storage

* ggml-openvino: invalidate a cached graph when its output set changes

* ggml-openvino: bound the compiled-model cache to N shapes instead of 1

* ggml-openvino: add GGML_OPENVINO_LOG_SUPPORTS_OP diagnostic

* ggml-openvino: honour a node's dynamic-dim classification on non-split graphs too

* ggml-openvino: fold consecutive SET_ROWS column writes into one scatter

* ggml-openvino: keep the speculative decoding feature buffers in device memory

* ggml-openvino: keep the fixed token count of static graph inputs for npu
GDN

In a static (NPU) graph that overwrites the fixed token count that
get_graph_input_shape set just before, for example of inp_tokens, so the NPU
graph got a dynamic token dimension. GATED_DELTA_NET models (Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6)
then fail to translate: "GATED_DELTA_NET pad masking requires a static token
dimension". Keep the change for dynamic graphs and the previous behaviour for
static ones.

items.name: b12658
items.body:
<details open>

rpc : typed request helpers and a single validation step on the server (#32651)

* rpc : typed request helpers and a single validation step on the server

Client and server share one table (rpc_msg_types) that maps each
fixed-size command to its request and response structs. The client sends
them with dispatcher->call<CMD>() and call_async<CMD>(), the server serves
them with rpc_serve<CMD>(), so the per-command code in rpc_serve_client
and at the call sites is gone and a wrong struct for a command does not
compile. SET_TENSOR, SET_TENSOR_2D and GRAPH_COMPUTE get header structs,
written with rpc_writer and parsed with a bounds-checked rpc_reader. The
wire format is unchanged.

Validation of client data is now in one place:
- deserialize_tensor rejects what ggml_new_tensor would assert on (op
  range, ne[0] not a multiple of the block size, element count overflow)
  and computes the tensor size without overflow before the buffer check
- rpc_check_region replaces the per-handler bounds checks and checks the
  request against the tensor size, which ggml_backend_tensor_set/get/memset
  assert on, so an in-buffer but out-of-tensor request no longer aborts
- graph_compute builds the graph in one pass over the tensors, which the
  client sends in topological order: no recursion, and unknown or
  duplicate ids, duplicate nodes, sources sent after their users, compute
  nodes with unallocated operands and views outside their view_src buffer
  are rejected; a tensor may be its own source (ggml_cast)
- GET_ALLOC_SIZE fails if a source tensor is invalid
- a client-sized allocation that fails closes the connection instead of
  terminating the server

* rpc : trim comments

</details>
